# Logo and end card

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

How the film signs off: the mark assembles, the lockup slides, the name cools, the frame keeps living. 40 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### End card replays the opening

`le-bookend-replay` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy any · any

The ending reuses the opening's stage and its mechanic, now carrying the brand, so the film closes on a rhyme the viewer has already learned.

- **Build:** Build the opening's stage (a Background component with an intensity prop) and its signature mechanic (a gap opening in a line, a word-roll, a mark slide, a window rise) as components with props, and call them again at the end with the same type size, position and curves. Run the mechanic mirrored, or with the brand as its payload. The window's exit is its entrance time-reversed: 1 - entrance(1 - t). The flanking words roll up and away (Words exit at half the stagger, E.in) and 'made with' plus the name roll in while the centre object holds. The opening's mark slide plays again, this time with the name. Bring the stage back only for brand beats: intensity 0 on product beats, then a 25 f rise from the bottom edge on E.out at the lockup. Never replay a reveal identically; the third use must add the name or the CTA.
- **Timing:** Word-roll: 28 f with a 5 f stagger. Mirrored exits keep the entrance's distance and duration. Stage rise: 25 f on E.out. Final hold: 96-120 f under the push.
- **Use when:** Films with a distinctive opening mechanic or stage. The signature move's third use. Loops, where the end hands back to frame 0.
- **Avoid when:** The opening was generic (replaying it only repeats a template). The reprise would be a frame-for-frame replay that adds nothing. Films under 10 s, where the rhyme has no time to land.

### Lockup keeps building through the hold

`le-living-hold` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy calm · any

Once resolved, the lockup never freezes: the card slowly pushes in (or exhales back), the tracking tightens a touch and the stage dims, so the last 1.5-2 s read as intentional rather than stalled.

- **Build:** Wrap the whole end card in one camera transform and push it about the lockup's optical centre with k = lmix(1, 1.15, prog(f, resolve, end, E.dolly)), a 10-20% push. Under that, tighten the name's letter-spacing from +0.03-0.06 em to its token track over 46 f on E.out, starting at its resolve. For a calm close, use the exhale instead: k = lmix(1, 0.9, prog(f, resolve, resolve + 120, E.out)) while only the stage dims to 35% over 36 f on E.smooth. The lockup stays at full strength to the last frame, because the last frame is the poster and never fades to black.
- **Primitive:** `lib/handoff.creep`
- **Timing:** Hold 90-120 f (1.5-2.0 s, never more than ~150 f). Push 10-20% over the hold on E.dolly. Tracking: 46 f on E.out. Exhale: 10% over 120 f on E.out, with a 36 f stage dim. Tail of at least 60 f after the last event, inside the hold.
- **Use when:** Every lockup and URL hold, and any card that must sit for more than 48 f.
- **Avoid when:** A designed freeze of at most 15 f on a silence (then stop everything, the push included). Loops whose hold must end at the frame-0 scale (ease the push back down instead).

### Logo cuts in oversized and settles

`dv-logo-oversize-land` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy medium · any

The mark or wordmark cuts in larger than its rest (1.3-1.9x), often defocused or tinted, and settles down with nearly half the move on the first frame; a square can jump 85 % in one frame and ease the rest over a long tail; a wordmark can resolve from a tint and blur, then drift away accelerating.

- **Build:** <Oversize from={1.4} dur={30} defocus> on the mark; Lockup snap for a one-frame jump. Anatomy: Scale 1.34-1.86x -> 1; blur peaks 3 f after entry then clears; colour tint -> ink (or a hue sweep). Sound: The voice saying the name 3 f after the picture; a snare on the jump.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Oversize`
- **Timing:** 28-62 f; 47 % of the travel in the first frame.
- **Use when:** Lockups, end cards, the brand's first appearance.
- **Avoid when:** Scaling the logo up from nothing.

### Snap on the hit, then the lockup slides

`le-mark-slide-name-follow` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy medium · launch, update · also `dv-lockup-snap-slide`

The mark shrinks a little, snaps to half its size in one frame on the hit, settles, then slides aside while the name rises in from the slide's middle; then everything locks.

- **Build:** lockupState(frame, { at, shrink: { frames: 3, to: 0.85 }, snap: { ratio: 0.5 }, settle: { frames: 9, ratio: 0.68 }, slide: { frames: 17, px }, wordmark: {} }) at 25 fps (scale the frames at other rates); <Lockup mark name />. The hit sound on lockupFrames().snap.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wordmark.lockupState`, `fx/Wordmark.Lockup`
- **Timing:** Shrink 3 f, snap 1 f, settle 9 f, slide 17 f peaking past the middle (M.lockup, peak about 86 px/f at 1080p), name 14 f, then a lock of 1 s or more.
- **Use when:** Every end card that has a mark and a name.
- **Avoid when:** The film's device should become the mark itself (then land it and slide only).

### Story object becomes the mark

`le-device-becomes-mark` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy any · any

The film's last object (a dot, circle, coin or pill) ends at exactly the mark's screen position and size, and the mark replaces it by a hard cut or an in-place morph, so the logo arrives as the answer to the story.

- **Build:** Compute the mark's final rect first (placeMark). Drive the story object so its last frame lands on that rect, or on 0.57 of it for the cut-and-grow ending, with matched centre, size, radius and colour. Examples: a coin turning rotateY 90 -> 10 deg on E.outSoft while it rises 20% of H; a word deleting from both ends (slice(k, n - k), k + 1 every 5 f) while its pill hugs the text down to a circle; a pill whose width collapses to the icon's rounded square (Morph on E.inOut). Then either hard-cut to the flat mark at exactly the object's last position and size (0.57 of the rect) and grow it lmix(0.57, 1, prog(f, cut, cut + 18, E.out)) about its centre, with half the growth in the first 2 f and no overshoot. Or finish in place: the dot's fill darkens to the mark's ink (mixColor over 12 f on E.smooth) and its glyph fades in over the last 4 f. Nothing may blink, double or change style across the seam, not even for one frame.
- **Timing:** Coin flip: 22 f on E.outSoft. Two-ended delete: 5 f per letter pair, pill width eased 4 f per step on E.ui. Pill-to-square morph: 30-40 f on E.inOut. Cut pop: 18 f on E.out (0.57 -> 1). In-place darkening: 12 f. Then hold ~20 f before the name follows.
- **Use when:** Every film that has a story device: the default way to arrive at the mark, especially as the device's third and final use.
- **Avoid when:** There is no recurring object (a mark forced out of an unrelated shape reads as a pun). The object's shape and the mark's disagree (a square into a circle needs a morph, never a cut).

### The mark assembles from alternating edges

`le-seed-stroke-build` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy medium · launch, update

The brand's own logo parts arrive from alternating frame edges on uneven gaps; long thin parts shoot in at constant speed and stop dead, panels arrive front-loaded, details pop last.

- **Build:** const logo = logoParts(svgText); const parts = assembleFor(logo, { start, x, y, size }, film); <AssembledMark logo parts x y size frame />. In a relief, extrude each part (pathPolys) as blocks under the key so the parts cast shadows as they land.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wordmark.assembleFor`, `fx/Wordmark.assembleState`, `fx/Wordmark.AssembledMark`, `brand/Mark.logoParts`
- **Timing:** Gaps 4/3/3/7/7/4 f at 24 fps (x2.5 at 60), stripes 6 f at 24 fps, panels 9 f.
- **Use when:** Any supplied logo with 3-8 parts.
- **Avoid when:** A one-shape logo: use the lockup slide or the swing.

### The one dead-still hold at the end

`dv-still-end-hold` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy calm · any

The film's only frozen frames are the end lockup: the card holds completely still for 1.2-3 s while the music drops out or a single final kick lands under it; a URL can pop on a sub-drop; the wordmark can scale in from 0.81 first; a split screen can hold one pane static while the others keep moving.

- **Build:** Recipe: a static end card from the timeline with no creep (declare the still range so the checks accept it). Anatomy: Zero drift (frame difference near 0); optional URL pop in one frame; optional plain entrance (4 blank frames, a 40 f linear fade). Sound: The music tail drops out (to about -42 LUFS) or a final kick; a cork pop and a sub-drop on the URL.
- **Timing:** Hold 73-220 f.
- **Use when:** Every end card.
- **Avoid when:** Fading to black under the hold; freezing anything earlier in the film.

### The product clears the stage

`le-stage-clears-to-brand` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy any · launch, feature, walkthrough

The last product element leaves (dropping out of frame, accelerating away, or bursting outward toward camera), and the brand, already waiting behind it, starts its reveal on the exact frame it is uncovered.

- **Build:** Keep the brand layer (stage plus lockup) mounted under the product for the whole shot, so the exit uncovers it instead of cutting to it. Exit the product one of three ways. (1) Time-reverse its own entrance with progress = 1 - entrance(1 - t); for a window this is typically a ~1000 px drop over 44 f on E.smooth. (2) Float a lone card up from its drift over 25 f on E.in while it grows 1 -> 1.33. (3) Burst a card cluster outward: each card translates 300-450 px along its vector from the cluster centre and scales lmix(1, 3) over 20 f on E.in, and the card layer is removed on the frame its fastest card passes ~75 px/f. Start the brand reveal on the frame the product's edge clears the lockup's box, computed from the exit curve. Either the mark grows lmix(0.48, 1, prog(..., E.out)) over 68 f, or a letterspaced wordmark (0.08 em) fades up over 40 f on E.smooth with no scale.
- **Timing:** Drop: 44 f on E.smooth (~1000 px, peak ~64 px/f, motion-blur pass on). Float-out: 25 f on E.in (5 -> 22 px/f, scale +33%). Burst: 20 f on E.in, cut at ~75 px/f. The brand reveal starts within 0-1 f of the clear frame. Mark growth: 68 f on E.out (edge speed ~17 px/f, no overshoot). Then hold 90-120 f under a 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs and feature films whose last shot is the product itself. The opening was a window or card entering, so the reverse bookends it. A crescendo of many screens that should give way to calm.
- **Avoid when:** The film's last beat is type, not product. A lockup that is already visible would be crossed by the exiting product. A burst with no build-up earlier to justify the energy.

### Wordmark built letter by letter

`le-letter-build-wordmark` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy calm · launch, update, sting, feature · also `dv-wordmark-letter-build`

The first letter grows from its baseline, the others fade in, slide home 2 frames apart and darken from a light grey to the ink, then the finished mark settles slightly smaller as one.

- **Build:** <Letters text="nsave" start mode="build" />: first letter M.letterGrow 7 f@30; the rest 2 f@30 apart, fade in 3.5 f, slide M.letterSlide 8 f, darken on E.stdInOut over 12 f; settle -9 % on E.glideOut over 20 f. Put one soft tick on each letter (thinned).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Letters`
- **Timing:** About 1.2 s to complete, settle 0.7 s; the lockup holds after.
- **Use when:** The wordmark of an end card; a product name introduced once.
- **Avoid when:** Any copy that has to be read (letters slow the read).

### Wordmark slides out of the mark

`dv-wordmark-slides-from-mark` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy calm · any

The mark travels aside to make room and the wordmark slides out from behind it, fading up from pale or revealed by a soft mask, and the whole lockup re-centres; after it lands the gap keeps closing until mark and word almost touch.

- **Build:** Lockup slide + Wipe gradient on the name, or Words with an x offset on E.snapOut. Anatomy: Slide 110-299 px cubic-out (38-42 % on the first step); wordmark opacity 0.3 -> 1 over 15 f, horizontally smeared at first; gap 20 -> 5 px in a slow tail. Sound: Often none (the music is in its tail). Materials: The wordmark can enter as a see-through wash: at 25-35 % opacity over the photo (the scene visible through the letters), doubled sideways by a ghost offset 20-30 px at half its opacity, turning solid brand colour as it slides 110-165 px into place over about 52 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wordmark`
- **Materials:** The wordmark can enter as a see-through wash: at 25-35 % opacity over the photo (the scene visible through the letters), doubled sideways by a ghost offset 20-30 px at half its opacity, turning solid brand colour as it slides 110-165 px into place over about 52 f.
- **Timing:** Slide 45-80 f; mask 20 f; gap tail 36 f.
- **Use when:** Every lockup that does not need a hit.
- **Avoid when:** The wordmark fading in place next to a static mark.

### Card shrinks to a pill, words close in

`le-card-to-pill-flank` · logo and end card · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

The last content card empties and shrinks into a small pill while the tagline words slide in from beyond the frame edges, blurred to sharp, to sit on either side of it; then the logo appears inside the pill.

- **Build:** Build a flex row [wordL][slot][wordR] and animate the slot's width from the card's width to the pill's width. Use Morph for the slot's box: radius to h/2, fill from the card surface to a solid tonal step of the stage. The words are then carried in from off-frame by the layout alone. Fade the card's content out over the first 6 f, before the slot moves fast, and shrink on E.whip. The words get blurIn(p, 8) and opacity prog(..., E.smooth), so they fly faded and resolve sharp on landing. When the pill lands, fade the Mark in inside it over 14 f on E.smooth. The row stays centred on the frame throughout.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Make the pill opaque: a solid tonal step of the stage (C.ink2 on C.ink, C.mist on C.paper), optionally with a 1.5 px C.line stroke. No translucent fill and no backdrop blur over the background. The full look relies on glass; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Content fade: 6 f. Shrink: 30 f on E.whip (card ~1240 -> ~310 px; each word travels ~470 px at a peak of ~58 px/f with the motion-blur pass on, faded until it lands). Logo fade: 14 f, starting 8 f after the pill lands. Then hold 90-120 f under a 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
- **Use when:** Films that opened with a gap or pill inside a headline (the reverse closes the bookend). Products whose output is a card, post, message or result. A tagline that brackets the brand: [wordL] [mark] [wordR].
- **Avoid when:** There is no card on screen to collapse. Words too long to fit beside the pill inside the safe width. Light-on-light stages where the pill loses its edge.

### CTA line closes its gaps

`le-accordion-cta-collapse` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

The end line starts with exaggerated spaces between its words, which close as the line settles centred; the last word, often the URL, travels farthest, so the eye ends there.

- **Build:** Lay the final line out centred. Give word i a start offset off_i = 70 + 80 * i px (capped at 290 px) in the direction of travel, so the last word travels farthest. Drive each word as x_i = finalX_i + off_i - inertia(f, a, off_i/14.6, 0.934).x: a pure exponential close with tau = 14.6 f and no overshoot (horizontal moves need no arrive). Enter on a hard cut from a larger line whose total width matches this line's stretched width. Optionally keep the URL soft for 8 f after it stops, then resolve it over 14 f with RackFocus, so focus is the last thing to settle.
- **Timing:** tau = 14.6 f: 55% closed in 10 f, 95% by 44 f. The last word starts at no more than 20 px/f and only slows from there. Gaps of ~150/115/80 px close to a normal word space (~0.25 em). URL focus: soft for 8 f, resolved over 14 f.
- **Use when:** A one-line CTA (a sentence plus a URL) after a large type beat. Type-led films whose last beat is a phrase locking together.
- **Avoid when:** Lines that wrap to two rows. Films that already closed a word gap earlier. Vertical frames where the stretched line would exceed the safe width.

### Device keeps time inside the lockup

`le-mark-ticks-in-lockup` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, loop, sting · also `dv-living-mark-sprite`

During the hold, the story device that became part of the mark (a dot, a bar, a stripe) gives one or two small ticks on the beat, so the bookend plays inside the finished lockup instead of after it.

- **Build:** Keep the device as its own Mark piece (e.g. MARK.D). During the hold, pulse only that piece: scale 1 + 0.12 * hitPulse(f - beat, 2, 6) about its own centre, or a nudge of 3 * hitPulse(f - beat, 2, 6) px along the device's signature direction. If the accent means 'what just landed', flash the piece to C.accent on the pulse and return it to its resting colour over 12 f with mixColor. Place 1-2 ticks on downbeats in the first second of the hold, in time with the stinger's tail, and none in the last 30 f, so the final frame is calm and identical to the poster.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Stepped`
- **Materials:** The pixel mark is drawn with 1-bit hatching: the body and wings are runs of diagonal and vertical 1 px stripes (an engraving rendered in pixels), cells 10-11 px at final size; it de-pixels through chunky solid cells into the hatched sprite (36 f), and 2 frames of each run cycle blend to 50 % grey cells.
- **Timing:** 1-2 ticks at least 30 f apart. hitPulse attack 2 f, tau 6 f (gone in ~38 f). Amplitude 10-14% scale or 2-4 px. None in the final 30 f.
- **Use when:** Films whose story device became a piece of the mark. Ends that should close the device's loop without ending on the device alone.
- **Avoid when:** Marks without a separable piece. Very still closes, where any pulse breaks the calm. Loops that need the device to travel back to its frame-0 position instead.

### End logo swells, then settles back

`dv-logo-swell-settle` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch, sting

The end logo grows a little past its rest (1.06 -> 1.22, or x1.4 with a decaying rate), then settles or slowly shrinks a few percent while the ground brightens.

- **Build:** Two tweens on the mark's scale (E.snapOut up, E.strongInOut down) or a reversal on the mark. Anatomy: Up on an ease-out, down on an in-out; background brightens over 60 f. Sound: The music drops out under it; a quiet tail.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Oversize`
- **Timing:** Up 26-38 f, down 30-44 f.
- **Use when:** The last beat of a film.
- **Avoid when:** Bounces.

### How the film leaves: fade, cut or defocus

`dv-end-exit` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · any

The last frames leave on purpose: the logo holds a third of a second and fades out on a sine over 20 f to a few black frames; or a hard cut to black on a drum hit with the tail ringing into silence; or the mark keeps receding and blurs out into silence.

- **Build:** Recipe: an opacity or defocus ramp on the end card group, aligned with the music's end. Anatomy: Fade 20 f sine; black 3-50 f; recede 0.3 %/f with a 38 f ease-in defocus. Sound: A sub-drop tail; a drum hit then silence; audio dropping to silence.
- **Timing:** 20-103 f.
- **Use when:** The final second of a film.
- **Avoid when:** An abrupt end with the music still running.

### Logo slams in on one blurred frame

`dv-logo-slam-frame` · logo and end card · accent · energy high · launch, sting

A big logo glyph fills its quadrant with a heavy motion blur on the last frame of a grid, moving diagonally: a one-frame slam.

- **Build:** A one-frame layer with a pre-blurred version of the glyph. Anatomy: One frame, blur along the direction of travel. Sound: None needed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** 2-3 f.
- **Use when:** Closing a grid section on a hit.
- **Avoid when:** More than one frame.

### Logo swing with anticipation

`le-slam-spin-pullout` · logo and end card · accent · energy high · launch, vertical · also `dv-logo-swing-in`

The mark swings back about 16 degrees, then springs past its rest (15-18 % over) while it shrinks from twice its size, settles and recedes slowly.

- **Build:** swingState(frame, { at, from, to: 0, back: 16, backFrames: 2, spring: SPR.logoSwing, scaleFrom: 2.14, tau: 12 }) at 24 fps; the one underdamped class of the film is the logo.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wordmark.swingState`
- **Materials:** Rotational smear on the fastest spin frames: the glyph inside the disc becomes a soft spiral ring and its tail is flung outside the disc as a comet (arc length about rotation speed x shutter x radius, about 100 deg at the peak); the rim becomes a soft band of the ground and the mark's colour; whites stay at full brightness. About 12 f of heavy smear, 12 of partial, sharp after.
- **Timing:** Back-swing 2 f, spring settle 18-22 f, scale tau 12 f (all at 24 fps).
- **Use when:** A playful or bold brand, one logo moment per film.
- **Avoid when:** A calm film: use the slide.

### Mark pops squashed and stretches to size

`dv-mark-squash-pop` · logo and end card · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

The mark appears on the frame after a dot at full width but 79 % height (108 % wide), and stretches to its true proportions over 6 frames: a landing with squash.

- **Build:** Recipe: separate scaleX and scaleY tweens on the mark. Anatomy: Height 0.79 -> 1 cubic-out over 12 f; width 1.08 -> 1 over 26 f. Sound: A kick.
- **Timing:** 12-26 f.
- **Use when:** Marks that land on a beat after a dot or a drop.
- **Avoid when:** Squash on type.

### Mark resolves in steps: de-pixel, ghost to ink, bold to final

`dv-mark-resolve-steps` · logo and end card · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A pixel-art mark appears as very coarse cells and resolves to finer cells while it zooms out; a glyph inside a notched square steps from ghost to white to ink; a symbol appears heavy with its counters filled and thins until the holes open, with small ticks radiating.

- **Build:** Pixelate in-phase on the mark; HardStep for the ghost-white-ink states; weight via two outline paths morphed (Morph path). Anatomy: Cells 55 -> 20 px near-linear; glyph states 3-4 f each; weight thinning over 34 f. Sound: A ding; a drum on the bold state. Materials: The symbol is a jagged upscaled bitmap until the snap: while big it shows hard pixel staircases with 2-3 grey anti-alias levels per step (a 40 px bitmap scaled with nearest-neighbour, cells about 14 px), and on the one-frame snap to half size on a drum hit it becomes the clean vector.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Pixel.Pixelate`
- **Materials:** The symbol is a jagged upscaled bitmap until the snap: while big it shows hard pixel staircases with 2-3 grey anti-alias levels per step (a 40 px bitmap scaled with nearest-neighbour, cells about 14 px), and on the one-frame snap to half size on a drum hit it becomes the clean vector.
- **Timing:** 16-75 f.
- **Use when:** Pixel or geometric marks.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth tweens for these steps.

### Mark turns through a key light

`le-mark-glint-turn` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch, sting, feature

The mark (an extruded glyph, a coin or a tile) turns a few degrees in 3D, and its face passes through a light, so a single specular sweep crosses it as it settles face-on.

- **Build:** Give the mark depth with CSS 3D: perspective 1200 px on the parent, the front face plus 6-10 copies stacked 1 px apart in z in a darker tonal step for the extrusion (or a mesh in Three.js). Rotate it rotateY tw(f, a, a+40, -35, 0, E.outSoft) with a small rotateX 20 -> 0 so it settles face-on. Sweep the light in 2D: a white band 30% of the mark's width, with opacity 0 -> 0.9 -> 0 across its width, masked to the mark (mask-image of the mark SVG) with mix-blend-mode screen, translated across the face over 14 f. Time it so the band's centre crosses as the rotation passes ~70%.
- **Timing:** Turn: 40 f on E.outSoft (~4 deg/f peak for 35 deg). Glint: 14 f on E.smooth, starting ~f20. One glint per film.
- **Use when:** Premium, material or physical brands (finance, hardware, collectibles). 3D marks. A mark that needs one moment of life early in its hold.
- **Avoid when:** Flat, playful or line marks (a sheen on a stroke looks like a template effect). Films with no other 3D. A second glint anywhere in the film (it reads as a preset).

### Name letters arrive hot and cool

`le-hot-to-neutral-cool` · logo and end card · accent · energy medium · launch, update · also `dv-hot-glyph-cool`

The name's letters arrive on the beat grid in the accent and cool to the type colour one after another, so the heat travels along the word.

- **Build:** <HotGlyphs text start every={6} accent ink cool={44} /> (born a paler step with `born` + `peak` if the accent is dark). One hue only; no bloom or halo unless the brand supplies a glow, and then a baked plate on haloLevel().
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Start the tile in the film's single accent as a flat fill, not a multi-hue gradient, and cool it through darker shades of that same hue to the neutral ink with mixColor. Any accent hue carries the idea, so it never needs a warm orange-to-red ramp. The full look relies on gradient, orange; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wordmark.hotGlyphState`, `fx/Wordmark.HotGlyphs`
- **Materials:** The halo travels with the newest letter: each new letter is born with a gradient fill (white to the accent across the glyph) and a two-layer glow (18 px and 60 px blur), wipes on with a left-to-right alpha ramp for 4 f, and cools to white over about 24 f; a soft radial halo about 350 x 260 px eases toward the newest letter at every step, so the glow is always on the head of the word.
- **Conditions:** light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo; gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** A letter every 6 f (16ths at 150 BPM), each cools over 44 f.
- **Use when:** A short name (3-8 letters) at the end card.
- **Avoid when:** Long names or taglines.

### Name types backwards, group stays centred

`le-reverse-type-recentre` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, sting, vertical

The name appears from its last letter to its first while the mark is pushed outward, so the lockup grows out of the mark's edge and stays centred on every frame.

- **Build:** Lay out [mark][gap][name], with every character laid out from the start and untyped characters at opacity 0. Measure each character's advance with measureTracked. Character i of n shows from frame t0 + 3.5 * (n-1-i), decided on fd, with a 4 f opacity ramp on E.ui, so the name grows leftward from its last letter. Keep the group centred without stepping: markLeft = cx - (markW + gap + ws(f))/2, where ws(f) = sum of adv_k * spr(f, t_k, SPR.firm) over the characters revealed so far. That is one critically damped spring per character, which glides the mark outward as each letter lands. If the story device is a dot, let it become the mark in place first: fill mixColor(C.mist, C.ink, p) over 12 f on E.smooth, with the glyph inside fading in over the last 4 f.
- **Timing:** 3.5 f per character (10 characters in 36 f), each fading in over 4 f on E.ui. Each width step eases on SPR.firm (no overshoot, ~20 f to settle). The mark travels ~270 px at 7-8 px/f on average. Dot-to-mark darkening takes 12 f. The lockup settles ~20 f after the last character, then holds 90-120 f under a 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
- **Use when:** Agent, assistant or persona products whose mark is an avatar or a disc. Names of 4-12 characters. A centred lockup that must never jump.
- **Avoid when:** Two-word names whose second word makes no sense on its own first. Right-to-left scripts (it becomes an ordinary type-on). The headline already used a typewriter.

### Staircase echo shape morph

`le-clone-stack-morph` · logo and end card · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A large brand shape collapses into a slim pill around the URL, and mid-morph its moving edges show stepped echoes from staggered copies, like a mechanical transformation.

- **Build:** Animate one rounded rect from the big shape to a pill that hugs the URL over 48 f on E.smooth, using morphBox from Morph.tsx or width, height and radius directly. Render 7 copies behind it: copy k samples the same morph at frame f - 2k and draws as a 1.5 px stroke (no fill) with opacity 0.6 * (1 - k/9) in one tonal step of the stage colour. The copies show only where the shape moves, stack into a staircase along the moving edges, and coincide and vanish once it rests. The URL swaps in at the start of the morph (8 f fade on E.smooth) and stays still once the pill lands.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Draw the echoes as plain 1.5 px strokes in one tonal step of the stage (C.ink2 on C.ink, C.line on C.paper) with a linear opacity falloff. No rim light, bloom or coloured edges on the copies. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MorphChain.MorphChain`
- **Timing:** Morph: 48 f on E.smooth, height 983 -> 227 px (edge peak ~22 px/f), width 1878 -> 997 px with a long tail. 7 copies at a 2 f delay each (14 f of echo after the leader stops). The URL stays readable for at least 102 f afterwards, under the card's 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
- **Use when:** Turning a big brand shape or frame into the CTA container. Mechanical, engineered or developer-tool brands. One moment that should feel designed rather than tweened.
- **Avoid when:** Short moves (under ~150 px the echoes collapse into a smear). Elements that already carry motion blur (double trails). More than once per film.

### Stop-motion brand strobe

`le-strobe-sting` · logo and end card · accent · energy high · sting, launch, loop, vertical

A burst of hard-cut brand states (the poster, the lockup tiled in ever denser grids, one flood, the boxed wordmark, the glyph) flickers past in under a second as a punchy sign-off.

- **Build:** After the lockup's hold, cut through an array of full-frame states with no interpolation: const seq = [[poster,7],[grid3,5],[grid4,5],[gridA,2],[gridB,2],[flood,5],[ink,5],[boxedName,5],[glyph,7]], accumulated into Sequences or chosen with fd(frame). The grids are a CSS grid of the lockup with n = 3, 4, 5, 5 columns and a half-tile offset on alternate states, so the cuts read as a stepped pull-back. Keep every state on the same dark stage, with the accent flood as the only bright state, so there are no more than 3 large light-dark flips per second. End on the glyph alone for at most 30 f, and export the poster from the lockup frame, not the last frame. A quiet version keeps only the last two states (boxed name 5 f, glyph 7 f) as a loop point.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Replace the cream flood with the film's single accent flood (or C.ink2), keep every other state on the dark stage, and allow only one bright state, so the strobe changes shape and density rather than luminance. The full look relies on beige; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Stepped.Stepped`
- **Timing:** Holds 7, 5, 5, 2, 2, 5, 5, 5, 7 f (43 f, ~0.72 s). Glyph ~2% of H, centred, for at most 30 f. A tick cluster under it that matches the opening's sound.
- **Use when:** Social stings and launch films with a poster-driven or stop-motion identity. A re-energising coda after a quiet end card. Autoplay loops that need a clean reset point.
- **Avoid when:** Calm or premium brands. Any film where you cannot keep large light-dark flips under 3 per second (photosensitivity). Any case where it would cut the lockup's hold below 1.5 s.

### Tracking tightens on arrival, collapses on exit

`le-tracking-tighten-collapse` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch, update, sting, feature · also `dv-tracking-collapse-exit`

A wordmark lands slightly open and its spacing closes about 3 % as it settles; to leave, its letters pull together fast and the mark is cut at speed.

- **Build:** Letters tracking={{ from: 0.024 }} (em a gap, closing over 10 f@30 on E.glideOut); collapse={{ at }} pulls the spacing to -0.5 em on E.buildIn over 5 f@30, then the word is cut (a velocity seam is declared on the next frame).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Letters`
- **Timing:** Tighten 0.33 s; collapse 0.17 s into the cut.
- **Use when:** A lockup that should feel assembled; an exit into a carried cut.
- **Avoid when:** Body copy; a lockup that must hold dead still.

### Wordmark letters blur-stagger in, a script suffix pen-writes

`dv-wordmark-soft-reveal` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch, sting

The icon scales in, then the wordmark letters reveal left to right (about 1.3 f per glyph), each from a blur or a pale tint to full; a script suffix writes on with a pen; a dot can run a rounded path with a hairline trail.

- **Build:** Letters build with FocusWord-style blur per letter; script as a stroke path with strokeDrawn(). Anatomy: Per letter blur 20 px -> 0 and fade over 3-4 f; script 16-28 f; settle 100 f; optional 90 f fade to black. Sound: Kicks under the icon; a whoosh on the exit; audio to silence. Materials: The end fade dims the white ground to grey and black while the floor glow keeps its colour a beat longer (the ground's brightness falls over 90 f, the glow's starts 20 f later), so the coloured light is the last thing besides the wordmark, which deepens to a dark shade of the accent.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Letters`
- **Materials:** The end fade dims the white ground to grey and black while the floor glow keeps its colour a beat longer (the ground's brightness falls over 90 f, the glow's starts 20 f later), so the coloured light is the last thing besides the wordmark, which deepens to a dark shade of the accent.
- **Timing:** Letters 22-24 f; script 16-28 f.
- **Use when:** Soft, friendly brands.
- **Avoid when:** Script suffixes in a brand without one.

### Wordmark types on a beat grid, lands loose and tightens

`dv-wordmark-type-on` · logo and end card · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

The wordmark's letters cut in one at a time on a grid locked to the music (every 8 f, triplets of the beat) or one per frame landing a little loose and tightening 3 %; a product mark resolves glyph by glyph with one glyph translucent and darkening in steps.

- **Build:** <Letters mode="pop" tracking> with starts on the beat grid. Anatomy: Letters cut on; landing +44 px loose, tightening over 10 f; one glyph darkening in steps. Sound: Letters within 23-33 ms of beats; a bubble pop at the end.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Letters`
- **Timing:** Letters every 1-8 f; tighten 20 f.
- **Use when:** A lockup for a product with a typed or technical feel.
- **Avoid when:** Off-grid letter timing.

### Words part, URL types into the gap

`le-words-part-url-types` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

The closing line splits at its middle, both halves slide outward and dim, the URL types letter by letter into the gap, and the flanks fade so the URL holds alone.

- **Build:** Set the closing line as two spans that meet at the centre. Split them apart by +/-(urlWidth/2 + 40 px) over 44 f on E.smooth, with colour mixColor(C.ink, C.mute, p) so they dim but stay legible. From 40% of the split, type the URL centred in the gap with TypeOn: 1 character per 4 f, head fade 4 f, caret hidden once done. After the last key, fade the flanks to 0 over 16 f on E.smooth. Keep the URL still on the card while the card pushes 10-15% on E.dolly; the mark then joins above it, or the URL becomes the lockup's secondary line.
- **Timing:** Split: 44 f on E.smooth over 250-300 px (peak 20 px/f or less). URL starts at 40% of the split, 4 f per character. Flank fade: 16 f after the last key. URL readable and still for at least 102 f.
- **Use when:** The closing line is a two-word phrase or pun built around the product, and the CTA is a URL. Minimal, type-only films.
- **Avoid when:** Lines longer than ~4 words. Films with no typing anywhere else (it would add a new device at the very end). URLs too long for the gap to open within the safe width.

### App icon de-blurs while its monogram writes and lines converge

`dv-icon-monogram-converge` · logo and end card · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

A rounded app-icon tile cuts in blurred at about 2.3x and shrinks to size while sharpening; inside it a monogram is written with a pen; about 16 curves draw in from the frame edges converging on it.

- **Build:** Oversize from 2.3 with defocus; the monogram path with strokeDrawn(); converging curves as SVG paths with dash growth. Anatomy: Icon settle 71 f; pen 26 f; lines with linear ink growth 66 f. Sound: Voice.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Oversize`, `fx/Stepped.strokeDrawn`
- **Timing:** Icon to size 28 f, settle 140 f.
- **Use when:** An app's end card.
- **Avoid when:** Too many converging lines (over about 20).

### Blobs fuse and split, then collapse into the mark

`dv-blob-fusion-mark` · logo and end card · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Two huge blobs enter from both edges, fuse into a gooey shape that shrinks and bulges, split into circles, approach again and repeat three times, shrinking each time, and collapse into the mark.

- **Build:** Recipe: an SVG gooey filter (a static blur + alpha threshold, built once) over two circles moved in closed form. Anatomy: Enter 149 px/f; fuse; split expo-out; approach expo-in; bulge +11 % area and a +12 % rebound. Sound: A drum at the fusion; a deep boom on the mark. Materials: The blobs are jelly, not perfect metaballs: in flight they stretch along their travel with flattened leading faces (rx = r(1 + kv), ry = r / (1 + kv), rotated to the heading); slowing, they become wobbling circles whose flat facet travels round the edge (r(1 + 0.06 sin(3 theta + 0.2 f))); they fuse, split and fuse again on hits before collapsing to the dot of the mark. Crisp edges, no blur or shadow; a goo filter (blur 18 then an alpha threshold) merges them.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MorphPath.Goo`
- **Materials:** The blobs are jelly, not perfect metaballs: in flight they stretch along their travel with flattened leading faces (rx = r(1 + kv), ry = r / (1 + kv), rotated to the heading); slowing, they become wobbling circles whose flat facet travels round the edge (r(1 + 0.06 sin(3 theta + 0.2 f))); they fuse, split and fuse again on hits before collapsing to the dot of the mark. Crisp edges, no blur or shadow; a goo filter (blur 18 then an alpha threshold) merges them.
- **Timing:** Cycles of 18-28 f; 90 f in all.
- **Use when:** A brand with round forms; an energetic end.
- **Avoid when:** More than three cycles.

### Brackets become strokes that shrink to dots as the logo grows

`dv-markers-collapse-to-logo` · logo and end card · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

At the last line the corner brackets turn into four diagonal strokes in an X around a centre dot, which shrink into small dots while the logo grows from the centre; one blink and the end card holds.

- **Build:** Markers rects morphed into diagonal strokes (rotated rects) then dots; Oversize from 0 is not allowed: the logo grows from the centre dot's size on E.snapOut. Anatomy: Strokes 90 -> 131 px then shrinking to 20-28 px dots; logo expo-out from the centre; one 1-frame blink. Sound: A sub-bass hit.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Markers`
- **Timing:** Strokes 28 f; logo 25 f.
- **Use when:** A film that used corner markers throughout: they hand over to the logo.
- **Avoid when:** Without a marker system earlier in the film.

### Colour blocks swarm into letter slots and become glyphs

`dv-block-swarm-to-wordmark` · logo and end card · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Coloured rectangles flash at scattered spots for two frames each, converge, become letter-sized placeholders in the wordmark's slots, and swap to glyphs one by one; the mascot fills in to black.

- **Build:** Build: <BlockSwarm at text x y font palette> (fx/Gather): one block per letter flashes at a seeded spot for two frames (4 f at 60), each pose nearer its slot (18 f), sits as a letter-sized placeholder (6 f), then the glyphs swap in left to right every 3 f; letterSlots() gives the boxes; fill the mascot with Develop or a tint. Anatomy: Blocks held 2 f at random spots; converge; placeholders in letter boxes; glyph swaps every 1-2 f. Sound: A whoosh, a bubble pop, a key click.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Gather.BlockSwarm`
- **Timing:** Swarm 18 f; swaps 2-4 f apart; fill 16 f.
- **Use when:** Playful brands with a palette; a wordmark reveal.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films.

### Light comets spiral out and collapse into the logo

`dv-comets-to-logo` · logo and end card · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Two point-symmetric light comets (a bright head, a curved tail) spiral out from the centre, orbit once and collapse into the logo's position at full speed, where the mark appears.

- **Build:** Build: <Comets at x y color> (fx/Gather) centred on the mark: two point-symmetric flat heads with tapering tails spiral out (10 f, E.snapOut, to 450 px), orbit (8 f) and collapse on E.buildIn (26 f), arriving at about 85 px per 30 fps frame; land the mark on cometsState().land. Ban-safe: no halo. Anatomy: Expand 10 f, orbit 8 f, collapse 26 f (radial 110 px/f at the end); tails 19-84 px. Sound: A run of whooshes, then a hit on the mark. Materials: The last word dims from white to grey over 14 f while its corner brackets shrink to small hooks; one frame after the dim ends two curved light comets appear crossing the word's centre and swing outward (head at full white, tail 20-85 px, a halo of about 150 px at 4-6 % over the stage, screen blend); the word's ghost stays faintly visible under them for 12 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Gather.Comets`
- **Materials:** The last word dims from white to grey over 14 f while its corner brackets shrink to small hooks; one frame after the dim ends two curved light comets appear crossing the word's centre and swing outward (head at full white, tail 20-85 px, a halo of about 150 px at 4-6 % over the stage, screen blend); the word's ghost stays faintly visible under them for 12 f.
- **Conditions:** light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo
- **Timing:** 34 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** A dark film's logo reveal.
- **Avoid when:** Light grounds; glow-heavy comets in house films.

### Liquid blob resolves into the mark

`le-gooey-merge-to-mark` · logo and end card · signature · energy medium · launch, sting, loop

A dot, or two soft lobes sliding in from the sides, swells into a liquid blob that stretches, splits and snaps into the crisp geometric mark.

- **Build:** Draw the mark's primitives as SVG circles and rects in one group, all starting stacked on the seed dot, and move each to its final place on E.smooth with a 2-4 f stagger. Two-lobe version: two large rounded shapes move translateX +/-600 -> +/-160 px on E.outSoft, fuse at centre and frame the closing line. Filter the group with feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 10, then feColorMatrix (type matrix, alpha row '0 0 0 18 -7'), which thresholds the blur into a liquid neck wherever parts are close. Over the last 8 f, ramp stdDeviation 10 -> 0. On the frame it reaches 0, swap the filtered group for the crisp Mark at the identical transform: a one-frame swap of identical shapes, never a crossfade. Use flat fills only; the threshold makes hard edges, and rim lights or inner highlights would be eaten or look like neon.
- **Timing:** 46 f. Parts travel f0-38 on E.smooth at a 2-4 f stagger, and the blob visibly splits ~26 f in. Blur ramp and crisp swap over the last 8 f. Two-lobe version: converge in 40 f on E.outSoft (first frame ~49 px/f, motion-blur pass on), then drift 0.3-0.5 px/f under the line.
- **Use when:** Products about raw input becoming structure, or about merging and joining. The story device is a dot. Marks made of a few separate primitives.
- **Avoid when:** Marks with thin strokes or text inside (the threshold eats them). Brands that need crisp precision throughout. Films already using a soft morph seam.

### Logo assembles from parts

`dv-logo-assemble-parts` · logo and end card · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

The mark builds from its parts entering from alternating edges with uneven gaps (panels front-loaded, thin parts as constant-speed stripes that stop dead, small details popping last); a custom round glyph assembles from arc pieces that grow along the circle.

- **Build:** <AssembledMark> / assembleFor(logo, ...). Anatomy: Gaps 4/3/3/7/7/4 f at 24 fps; panels 7-12 f expo-out each; arcs 14 f. Sound: A pop on each main part.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wordmark`
- **Timing:** 14-92 f.
- **Use when:** Logos made of geometric parts.
- **Avoid when:** Even gaps (they read mechanical).

### Logo grows out of a line, a bar, a pixel monogram

`dv-logo-build-chain` · logo and end card · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

The mark is reached through a chain of simple states: a hairline fades in, grows into a tall bar that splits into stripes, the stripe stack squashes (anticipation) and each stripe slides sideways into the pixel mark; or two dots grow into a pixel monogram glyph by glyph, which collapses into a bar, which becomes the symbol.

- **Build:** MorphChain with explicit states (line, bar, stripes, mark) and HardStep for the stripe offsets; logoParts() for the final mark. Anatomy: Fade 8 f (63 % in the last frame); grow 28 f; squash -5 % then -30 %; stripes slide 23 f on an S-curve; monogram build 38 f, collapse 8 f, bar 1 f. Sound: A reverse-cymbal swell bed; a pluck on the slide; a drum on the build.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MorphChain`
- **Timing:** 45-82 f.
- **Use when:** Brands with a geometric or pixel mark; the opening or the closing of a film.
- **Avoid when:** Chains longer than four states.

### Pull out of the mark, undershoot, breathe

`le-macro-pullout-breathe` · logo and end card · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature, vertical

The mark arrives so large that only fragments of it fill the frame, collapses to slightly smaller than its final size, then gently breathes up to rest, as if the camera had found it.

- **Build:** Place the Mark with placeMark at its final spot; centre it where the lockup needs it, e.g. 80 px left of frame centre to leave room for the name. Pick the start scale s0 so the mark's outer edge starts about 750 px from its centre (s0 = 750 / the mark's half-width at rest, about 5x for a 300 px mark), so only fragments fill the frame. Scale it about its own centre in log space: s = lmix(s0, 0.93, prog(f, a, a+N, E.outSoft)) * lmix(1, 1/0.93, prog(f, a+N-24, a+N, E.smooth)), with N = 43 x ln(s0 / 0.93) frames (72 f from 5x). The log rate then starts near 0.105/f, so the outer edge never passes about 80 px/f; from 5x it crosses 1.0 near f35, bottoms out at 0.94 near f52 and breathes up to rest at 1.0 by f72 with no velocity step. Enter it on a cut: the outgoing shot shrinks into its centre on E.in over its last 24 f and cuts at a matching log speed (or start from zoomHandoff in camera.ts at the outgoing log speed). Render with the motion-blur pass. Keep the mark's counters and small parts outside the frame until the log rate falls below 0.07/f (~f10). Put the bottom of the undershoot on the strongest low hit after a ~15 f bass gap.
- **Timing:** Collapse: N = 43 x ln(s0 / 0.93) frames on E.outSoft (72 f from 5x; log rate about 0.105/f at the start, outer edge under about 80 px/f, under 0.07/f by f10). Breathe: the last 24 f on E.smooth (0.93 -> 1.0), bottoming at 0.94 near f52. Settled by f72. Hold the mark ~20 f before the name follows.
- **Use when:** The mark's first full appearance at the end, or a logo sting. A hit after a short bass gap. Marks with a strong silhouette or inner shapes that read as abstract fragments when huge.
- **Avoid when:** Thin line marks (at macro scale they become two hairlines crossing the frame). Right after another zoom-through seam. The mark was already shown at hero size earlier (that makes this a replayed reveal).

### Start inside the mark and pull back to it

`dv-pull-back-from-mark` · logo and end card · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Hard cut to the inside of a huge 3D mark; the camera pulls back about 12x with a roll (the first frame halves the size, the ratio relaxing after), then snaps to the flat mark.

- **Build:** zoomThrough in reverse (factor 1/12) with roll; HardStep to the flat mark. Anatomy: Pull back in log space, roll, final snap to the flat version. Sound: Kick, snare, kick across the pull.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** 76 f + 34 f.
- **Use when:** The end of a film whose mark has a 3D form.
- **Avoid when:** Marks without a recognisable silhouette.

### The mark lands inside a window of a real photograph

`dv-mark-in-photo-window` · logo and end card · signature · energy calm · launch

The logo is not set on a flat ground: it spins in exactly inside the window glass of a warm photograph (a train window onto a mountain lake), sitting on the horizon, with the rest of the photo softly out of focus round it and a very slow push.

- **Build:** Photo framed on the window, a second blurred copy masked outside it, and the lockup placed in the window's rect. Anatomy: The window area sharp, the foreground and top blurred 12-18 px (a tilt-shift from two masked copies); the mark about 146 px across, centred on the horizon at 52 % of the window's height; push about 1 % over the beat. Sound: Spin-in on a whoosh; wordmark on the next hit. Materials: Choose a free photo whose window or frame is the composition; grade it toward the brand's ink so the mark owns the brightest colour.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Photo`
- **Materials:** Choose a free photo whose window or frame is the composition; grade it toward the brand's ink so the mark owns the brightest colour.
- **Timing:** Holds about 90 f; the wordmark follows on the next hit.
- **Use when:** A consumer brand with a place or a feeling; the end card of a lifestyle film.
- **Avoid when:** Developer tools; busy photos without a calm window area.

### The supplied mark cast in the film's relief

`le-relief-device-lockup` · logo and end card · signature · energy medium · launch, update

The brand's logo, supplied as SVG, is cast in the same lit relief as the film: its parts slide in from alternating edges and stop dead with their shadows, the part that plays the film's device rises and takes the accent, then the mark slides aside and the name arrives hot, printed raised on the floor.

- **Build:** logoParts(svg) -> per part pathPolys() -> ReliefScene blocks (h 20-30 px; the device part rises to 60-80 px on E.snapOut); offsets from assembleFor(); lockupState().x slides the blocks; the name as raised floor type with hotGlyphState colours; the key moves slowly through the hold (azimuth +15-25 deg) so the end lock is alive without a glow.
- **Primitive:** `fx/KeyLight.ReliefScene`, `brand/Mark.logoParts`, `brand/Mark.pathPolys`, `fx/Wordmark.assembleFor`, `fx/Wordmark.lockupState`, `fx/Wordmark.hotGlyphState`
- **Timing:** Assembly about 1.3 s, the device rise 30 f, the slide 34 f, the name a letter every 5 f.
- **Use when:** A film built as a relief or with a key-lit world; any supplied mark without holes or with simple parts.
- **Avoid when:** Logos with fine detail under 2 % of the mark (they become slivers in relief).
